//ConnectionStrings: Passwords come from Google Secret Manager or environment variables / user-secrets — never commit real credentials. The provider selected by 'DatabaseProvider' picks the matching entry: Sqlite→SqliteConnection, Sqlserver→DefaultConnection, Postgres→PostgresConnection, Mysql→MySqlConnection.
//UseSharedMachineDatabase: When true, the API adopts the DatabaseProvider + SqliteDatabasePath written to %LocalAppData%\VaultGuard\settings.json by the WPF/Web apps so all VaultGuard apps on one machine share a vault. Leave false for server deployments.

ApiSettings.Title: Vault Guard API
ApiSettings.Description: A comprehensive password management API with sync capabilities

//GoogleSecretManager: Secrets management (production defaults; dev overrides in appsettings.Development.json). Auth uses Application Default Credentials — an attached service account on GCP (grant it roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor), or `gcloud auth application-default login` / a GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS key file locally; no credentials are committed. Load is scoped to secrets labelled env=prod. Store db parts as secrets 'dbserver', 'dbusername', 'dbpassword' (composed into a SQL Server connection string). Other secrets use '__' for nesting, e.g. JwtSettings__SecretKey, Sentry__Dsn. They override the values below at startup. Optional=false = fail-closed: startup aborts if the vault can't be read, so prod never runs on placeholder credentials.
